divergences.what: Volta (sm_70) arm for the GDN tensor-core path (branch m2-volta-gdn)
divergences.kernel_body_changes: Only two preprocessor lines inside gdn_single differ from the pinned body: the arch gate admits (!__HIPCC__ && VOLTA_MMA_AVAILABLE) alongside AMPERE/HIP-RDNA3, and the tile width N is 16 under the same condition (as on HIP). Every other body line is byte-identical; the kernel_body_sha256 above still pins the unextended upstream body.
divergences.adapter_additions: All other changes are in the local adapter around the body, guarded by #if !defined(__HIPCC__) && defined(VOLTA_MMA_AVAILABLE) (the macro comes from the pinned ggml common.cuh, __CUDA_ARCH__ == 700): a local m8n8k4 tile layer (vfrag/vfrag_a/vfrag_b/vtile and an mma() wrapper issuing mma.sync.aligned.m8n8k4.row.col.f32.f16.f16.f32, the V100-measured fragment/C mapping documented in src/kernels/cuda/qsa_prompt_attn.cu; the wrapper re-aligns the warp with __syncwarp() first, since mma.sync.aligned needs every lane arrived and Volta's independent thread scheduling does not guarantee reconvergence after the kernel's lane-divergent q/k prefetch reads and forward substitution) instead of the untouched ldmatrix helpers; per-thread fragment gathers in load<>() from plain row-major shared memory (the HIP arm's layout); FP16 hi/lo residual storage in matrix::store/store2 (Volta has no BF16; 11+11 mantissa bits carry the residual scheme, and the host preprocessing keeps every operand inside FP16's exponent range, so no qsa-style pre-scaling was needed), with a local __bfloat162float(__half) overload so the body's residual read-back compiles unchanged. Host dispatch: gdn_mma_policy.hpp admits (7,0) only under STRATA_EXPERIMENTAL_SM60, so the ready-made engine keeps byte-identical behavior.
